filter_note: V1 set (7) + market briefing + AI news; Today window = Mon Nov 23 (after the morning run) – Tue Nov 24 morning PT (items already on the Nov 20 and Nov 23 briefs not re-led)

market_briefing.lede: Approval policies and data controls became the product on Monday: Anthropic shipped agents that review, fix and approve pull requests under a team-written policy, and opened a Bedrock route that keeps retained prompts for its top models in the customer's own AWS account.

bullets.text: Nov 23: Claude Ship (beta, Team and Enterprise, GitHub) pairs Code Review with PR Steward, which fixes failing checks and review feedback but is designed not to approve or merge, and Claude Approvals, which approves only what a repository policy file allows; Anthropic recommends starting in observe-only mode.

Nov 23: AWS made its Bedrock trusted access program API generally available and put Anthropic's Enterprise Frontier Safeguards in public preview: retained prompts and completions for Claude Fable, Mythos and CVP models go to the customer's S3 bucket under the customer's KMS key, and flagged activity arrives as cases for the customer's own team to review.

Nov 23: OpenAI's OpenWorks pilot in 20 US communities funds local AI experts (stipends up to $8,000 a month) to set up AI for small businesses at no cost to them, including three months of ChatGPT Business.

biggest_ai_news.title: ANT falls below its $83 IPO price
biggest_ai_news.body: Nov 24: Anthropic shares fell 12% in Tuesday trading, dropping below the $83 offer after opening at $111.50 on debut day; Canaccord (buy, $135), Oppenheimer (outperform, $150) and Wedbush (outperform, $120) started coverage Monday–Tuesday.

biggest_ai_news.title: Anthropic lets enterprises keep frontier-model data in their own cloud
biggest_ai_news.body: Nov 23: enterprise frontier safeguards keep Anthropic's 30-day retention rule for Mythos and Fable but let customers hold the data, and the encryption keys, in their own cloud; Anthropic says it built the system with more than 100 customers. The first route is Amazon Bedrock (public preview).

biggest_ai_news.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship for pull requests
biggest_ai_news.body: Nov 23: Claude can now review, fix and, where a repository's policy allows, approve pull requests; billed on tokens with per-repository spend limits, and not available to orgs on Zero Data Retention, HIPAA or customer-managed keys.

biggest_ai_news.title: OpenAI ships a ChatGPT-tuned GPT-6.2 Sol
biggest_ai_news.body: Nov 23: a chat-specific version of GPT-6.2 Sol, which OpenAI says handles complex, detailed requests and web lookups better, is rolling out to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise.

what_changed.title: Salesforce Contact Centre reaches general availability in Australia and New Zealand
what_changed.body: Nov 24: the native contact centre (AI agents including Fin, human reps, voice, digital channels and CRM data on one platform) is now GA in ANZ, after North America in March and Europe in October. Salesforce says it is used in 68 countries and that headless skills now let teams set it up conversationally from AI coding assistants like Claude or Cursor without logging into Salesforce.

what_changed.title: Anthropic and AWS open customer-held retention for Anthropic's top models
what_changed.body: Nov 23: the Bedrock trusted access program API is GA; Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (data in the customer's S3 bucket and KMS key) and Enterprise Data Controls (Amazon-managed storage) are in public preview. Current Fable models keep a zero-data-retention exception for internal use through at least June 30, 2027.

what_changed.title: Claude Ship puts PR approval under a team-written policy
what_changed.body: Nov 23: PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta for Claude Team and Enterprise on GitHub; Code Review is GA. Eligible Enterprise orgs can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits by Jan 15, 2027.

what_changed.title: OpenAI funds local partners to bring ChatGPT to small businesses
what_changed.body: Nov 23: OpenWorks is recruiting its first partners; the pilot covers 20 US communities and excludes software/SaaS, venture-backed and PE-owned businesses.

what_changed.title: Clay ships a batch of credit and enrichment fixes
what_changed.body: Nov 24: in a Make It Great Week post Clay listed 67 shipped tickets, including no credit charge when a Crunchbase funding lookup comes back empty, a label showing which third-party enrichments cost zero credits, G2 lookups for vendor products, prices paid and contract lengths, and phone lookups that stop when providers repeat the same number.

quiet_note: No launch, funding, M&A or pricing of their own from Gong, Nooks, Outreach, Salesloft or Monaco dated Nov 23–24. Clay's Nov 23 blog is a lead-scoring how-to; Monaco's Nov 22–23 blog posts are explainers.

market_direction.label: Accelerating (policy-gated agent approvals)
market_direction.text: Claude Approvals approves pull requests only as a repo policy allows (Nov 23), following Close's pre-approved tools (Nov 21) and Coworker's approve-before-save edits (Nov 23).

market_direction.label: New (customer-held retention for frontier models)
market_direction.text: Anthropic's top models can now keep required 30-day logs in the customer's own AWS account (Nov 23), a week after Clay's bring-your-own Bedrock connection (Nov 20).

market_direction.label: Accelerating (headless setup of CRM products)
market_direction.text: Salesforce says Contact Centre can be configured from Claude or Cursor without logging into Salesforce (Nov 24).

market_direction.label: Steady (Gong, Nooks, Outreach, Salesloft, Monaco)
market_direction.text: No new announcements of their own Nov 23–24.

language_pulse.gloss: Anthropic's term for the repository file that tells Claude Approvals which pull requests it may approve on its own (Nov 23).
AWS's name for provider programs on Bedrock that trade stricter terms for more control over safety review and data storage (Nov 23).
Salesforce's term for setting up Contact Centre from AI coding assistants instead of the Salesforce UI (Nov 24).

competitive_moves.text: Salesforce Contact Centre GA in Australia and New Zealand; setup via headless skills from Claude or Cursor (Nov 24).
Make It Great Week: 67 fixes, including zero credits on empty Crunchbase lookups and zero-credit labels on enrichments (Nov 24).

watch.title: Wed Dec 2: Salesforce Q3 FY27 results
watch.body: Date conflict resolved: Salesforce's LinkedIn post has been edited and now says December 2 at 2 p.m. PT, matching the IR release (results after the close, call 2:00 PM PT). First quarter with the $50/user Coworker SKU (Nov 4), the Cresta deal (Nov 2), Copilotforce (Nov 17) and Coworker in the SMB suites (Nov 23).

interpretation.fact: Nov 24 Salesforce Contact Centre became GA in Australia and New Zealand. Nov 23 Anthropic launched Claude Ship (Code Review GA; PR Steward and Claude Approvals beta); AWS made the Bedrock trusted access program API GA with Anthropic's Enterprise Frontier Safeguards and Enterprise Data Controls in public preview; OpenAI launched the OpenWorks small-business pilot and a ChatGPT-tuned GPT-6.2 Sol. Nov 24 Clay listed 67 shipped fixes including zero-credit empty Crunchbase lookups; ANT fell 12% to below its $83 IPO price. Gong, Nooks, Outreach, Salesloft and Monaco announced nothing new of their own Nov 23–24.
interpretation.interpretation: Enterprise buyers are getting written policies and customer-held logs as the condition for letting agents act on their own; vendors that can show who approved an action, and where the record of it sits, will have an easier security review. OpenAI paying local partners to set up ChatGPT for small businesses is a bid for the same small-team buyers Salesforce just gave free Coworker access.

feed.summary: Clay shipped 67 fixes for Make It Great Week, including zero credits for empty Crunchbase funding lookups, G2 product and pricing lookups, and a label showing which enrichments cost zero credits.
